newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end lower ahead of central bank data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end lower ahead of central bank data.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower in moderate trade on Monday as investors took profits on some key stocks and awaited the release of key economic indicators, brokers said.

"Short-term local investors sold key stocks today after they bought them last week. The selling came as they await key economic indicators to be released by the central bank later this week," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
The SET index ended 5.62 points lower at 742.08 on 5.1 billion baht turnover. The market also traded in a narrow range, following other markets in the region, brokers said.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.59 point to 54.98.
Decliners led gainers 181 to 115 while 100 issues unchanged.
"They're also waiting for 1996 earning results of some major firms. The deadline of announcing the results is on Friday," said Thanadech.
Brokers said investors stayed on the sidelines today as they saw some of the regional markets such as Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia move sluggishly.

Large capitalised Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 174. Finance One dropped 0.25 to 27.50 while Advanced Info Services slipped eight to 244 and United Communication Industry unchanged at 164.
Support is seen by some brokers at 731-point and resistance at around 760 on Tuesday.
